subject: history
title: From villages to the Indus cities

scenes.narration: In the Neolithic Age, many people settled in small villages and practised agriculture. With better methods, surplus food was produced.

Gradually, villages grew into towns, and towns into cities; and the first great civilisations of the world were born. Civilisation is said to occur when a society is in an advanced state of social development.

nodes: City: a large and densely populated area
Urbanisation: more and more people move from villages to towns and cities
props.label: p.27

scenes.narration: A city is a large and densely populated area. When more and more people start moving from villages to towns and cities, the process is called urbanisation.
The Indus Valley Civilisation grew slowly from village communities between 7000 and 5000 BCE. It reached a highly developed phase with many large urban centres between 2,600 and 1,900 BCE.
